purpose: Teriflunomide is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the worsening of the disease. It does not cure MS, but it helps keep it under better control.
how_it_works: Your immune system normally protects you from germs, but in MS it mistakenly attacks the protective covering around your nerves. Teriflunomide works by slowing down the growth of certain immune cells that are causing this damage. Think of it as turning down the volume on the overactive part of your immune system so it stops attacking your nerves as aggressively.
common_side_effects: Hair thinning or hair loss (usually temporary), nausea, diarrhea, headache, tiredness, and tingling or numbness in your hands or feet. You may also notice your liver blood tests go up slightly, which is why your doctor will monitor your blood regularly.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems, so your doctor will check your liver with blood tests regularly. It must NOT be taken if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects. Both men and women need to use reliable birth control while taking it. Because it stays in your body for a long time, a special elimination procedure (using cholestyramine or activated charcoal) may be needed if you need to stop the medication quickly, such as before pregnancy. It can also lower your ability to fight infections, so tell your doctor right away if you develop a fever or signs of infection.
typical_dosing: Teriflunomide comes as a tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. The usual dose is either 7 mg or 14 mg daily, as prescribed by your doctor. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep it consistent.
